{"parentUuid":"5f8f2637-8087-44c8-a13c-5723454708b8","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_20261015.md","snippet":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n2\t\n3\tRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\n4\tRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n5\t\n6\t## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n7\t\n8\tI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editor would be the coach and captains, respectively where they have different permissions (captains can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They both would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers instantly. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n9\t\n10\tThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out suggested features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting.\n11\t\n12\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n13\t\n14\tTicket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so it was essentially forced to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3.\n15\t\n16\t## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n17\t\n18\tThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements.\n19\t\n20\tAdditionally, I went to bed after the first session where I implemented tickets T01-T03, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning.\n21\t\n22\t## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n23\t\n24\tPlann:\n25\tSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a ;5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n26\t\n27\tActual:\n28\t7 tickets that used about 54% of a 5 hour window in total spread across sessions. When taking into account grill, setup, and handoffs, about 116% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main sessions. This came in well under the forcast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n29\t\n30\t\n31\t\n32\t## 5. Future improvements\n33\t\n34\tThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. These should all be improved before actual use of the site.\n35\t\n36\tAdditionally, the site still runs on placeholders for admin and editor, so real accounts should be created for the coach and captain, which would also solve the issue of the passwords being committed in the transcript"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"804928fc-860a-47bb-a2d1-6a58d096d0bb","timestamp":"2026-10-15T19:31:18.097Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nNote: /home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_20261015.md changed on disk since you last read it. They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes.","originalFile":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\nRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n\n## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n\nI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editor would be the coach and captains, respectively where they have different permissions (captains can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They both would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers instantly. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n\nThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out suggested features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting.\n\n## 2. {"parentUuid":"367f9602-c01f-4663-b62d-15b3f67b20e6","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"5a21a765-7832-4372-8499-d632ea739d6e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0194cCdRqw9UA92NXKrUVaax","type":"tool_result","content":"1:# CMS Content Model, Roles, and Publishing: Research Notes\n3:## Summary\n9:## Glossary\n30:## Content Model\n32:### WordPress\n36:**Post Meta**: [Additional data is stored in the `wp_postmeta` table as unstructured key-value pairs, allowing arbitrary metadata attachment without schema changes.](https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/posts/post-meta/)\n38:**Taxonomies**: [WordPress provides two built-in taxonomies—categories (hierarchical) and tags (flat)—and allows custom taxonomies.](https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/taxonomies/) Terms are stored in the `wp_terms` and `wp_term_taxonomy` tables.\n40:### Drupal\n48:### Static-Site Generators\n58:## Users & Roles\n60:### WordPress\n63:- **Super Admin**: Network administration (multisite only)\n64:- **Administrator**: Full site access\n65:- **Editor**: Publish, edit, and moderate posts\n66:- **Author**: Publish and edit own posts\n----\n# CMS field notes\n\nNotes\n- when logging in as an editor, the users area is now missing from the wordpress sidebar. Not allowed to list users.\n- it says \"You need a higher level of permission. Sorry, you are not allowed to list users.\"\n- on top of hiding the users page from the editor, when you try to access it through the link, it denies you. So it goes beyod just hiding the page.\n- Publishing takes two clicks, which felt unnecessary\n- status filter is easy to miss and separate from the other filter that separates by date and category, which made the status filter confusing to find.\n- navigating to the wordpress dashboard was not straightforward in the first instance as I found myself a bit confused how to access all pages and posts.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"302a0bcf-acb1-4c82-ab37-3a6395810bce","timestamp":"2026-10-15T19:33:59.250Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"1:# CMS Content Model, Roles, and Publishing: Research Notes\n3:## Summary\n9:## Glossary\n30:## Content Model\n32:### WordPress\n36:**Post Meta**: [Additional data is stored in the `wp_postmeta` table as unstructured key-value pairs, allowing arbitrary metadata attachment without schema changes.](https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/posts/post-meta/)\n38:**Taxonomies**: [WordPress provides two built-in taxonomies—categories (hierarchical) and tags (flat)—and allows custom taxonomies.](https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/taxonomies/) Terms are stored in the `wp_terms` and `wp_term_taxonomy` tables.\n40:### Drupal\n48:### Static-Site Generators\n58:## Users & Roles\n60:### WordPress\n63:- **Super Admin**: Network administration (multisite only)\n64:- **Administrator**: Full site access\n65:- **Editor**: Publish, edit, and moderate posts\n66:- **Author**: Publish and edit own posts\n----\n# CMS field notes\n\nNotes\n- when logging in as an editor, the users area is now missing from the wordpress sidebar. Not allowed to list users.\n- it says \"You need a higher level of permission. Sorry, you are not allowed to list users.\"\n- on top of hiding the users page from the editor, when you try to access it through the link, it denies you. {"parentUuid":"db9c911d-c648-42bb-87cb-4d4d36e80d2e","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_20261015.md","snippet":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n2\t\n3\tRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\n4\tRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n5\t\n6\t## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n7\t\n8\tI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editor would be the coach and captains, respectively where they have different permissions (captains can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They both would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers instantly. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n9\t\n10\tThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out suggested features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting.\n11\t\n12\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n13\t\n14\tTicket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so it was essentially forced to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3.\n15\t\n16\t## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n17\t\n18\tThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n19\t\n20\tThe matt pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The Ai questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n21\t\n22\tAdditionally, I went to bed after the first session where I implemented tickets T01-T03, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n23\t\n24\t## 4. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n7\t\n8\tI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editor would be the coach and captains, respectively where they have different permissions (captains can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They both would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers instantly. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n9\t\n10\tThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out suggested features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting.\n11\t\n12\t## 2. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so it was essentially forced to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3.\n15\t\n16\t## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n17\t\n18\tThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine"," ","-I build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editor would be the coach and captains, respectively where they have different permissions (captains can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They both would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers instantly. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.","+I build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests."," ","-The grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out suggested features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting.","+The grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time)."," "," ## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it"," ","-Ticket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so it was essentially forced to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3.","+Ticket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004)."," "," ## 3. {"parentUuid":"fc6ce1a9-bd56-4216-a03c-2f28386aa589","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ecabb648-a68d-4179-99c2-c0e4f38b4e55","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01V9ZxzAFKsxPsAKjJurX5e1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n2\t\n3\tRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\n4\tRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n5\t\n6\t## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n7\t\n8\tI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n9\t\n10\tThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time).\n11\t\n12\t## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n13\t\n14\tTicket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004).\n15\t\n16\t## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n17\t\n18\tI first logged into WordPress to get a handle of what I was working on, and took note of what I found clunky, redundant, or what could maybe be improved upon. This was then used in the grill with docs session to generate actionable tickets.\n19\t\n20\tThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n21\t\n22\tThe matt pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The Ai questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n23\t\n24\tAdditionally, I went to bed after the first session where I implemented tickets T01-T03, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n25\t\n26\t## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n27\t\n28\tPlann:\n29\tSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a ;5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n30\t\n31\tActual:\n32\t7 tickets that used about 54% of a 5 hour window in total spread across sessions. When taking into account grill, setup, and handoffs, about 116% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main days (Oct 14 and 15). This came in well under the forcast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n33\t\n34\t\n35\t\n36\t## 5. Future improvements\n37\t\n38\tThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. These should all be improved before actual use of the site.\n39\t\n40\tAdditionally, the site still runs on placeholders for admin and editor, so real accounts should be created for the coach and captain, which would also solve the issue of the passwords being committed in the transcript"}]},"uuid":"6a72b6a2-341c-4aac-b5c0-612bc4516424","timestamp":"2026-10-15T19:42:01.884Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_20261015.md","content":"# IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\nRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n\n## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n\nI build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.\n\nThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n\nTicket 07 wwas built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004).\n\n## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n\nI first logged into WordPress to get a handle of what I was working on, and took note of what I found clunky, redundant, or what could maybe be improved upon. This was then used in the grill with docs session to generate actionable tickets.\n\nThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n\nThe matt pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The Ai questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n\nAdditionally, I went to bed after the first session where I implemented tickets T01-T03, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n\n## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n\nPlann:\nSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a ;5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n\nActual:\n7 tickets that used about 54% of a 5 hour window in total spread across sessions. When taking into account grill, setup, and handoffs, about 116% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main days (Oct 14 and 15). This came in well under the forcast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n\n\n\n## 5. Future improvements\n\nThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine"," ","-I build a wordpress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the github pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickes and 191 tests.","+I built a WordPress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the GitHub Pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickets and 191 tests."," ","-The grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's reccomendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time).","+The grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's recommendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). Sample 3 closed tickets; map each acceptance criterion to tests. Measure file lengths; look for large commented-out blocks. Run the seed script from `.env.example`.\n\n**T6 — Public site (F1, F2, S1.7).** Fetch the Pages URL over HTTPS; crawl all internal links; grep the `gh-pages` branch for `href=\"/` and `src=\"/`.\n\n**T7 — Prose review (A1–A4, G1–G2).** Read the report, the README statement, the field notes, `CONTEXT.md`, and the grill transcripts. Your rubric already describes exactly how the professor's agent grades: §10 has worker tasks T0–T7, and §9 gives the report format. A rehearsal is mostly a matter of copying that setup. Here's how:\n\n## 1. Save the report to GitHub, but don't tag yet\n\nThe grader works from what's on GitHub. Say \"push\" and I'll commit and push the report. Don't create `mp2-final` until after the rehearsal, so you can still fix what it finds without moving the tag.\n\n## 2. Grade a fresh clone, not your working folder\n\nThe real grader never sees your `.env`, your `cms.db`, or this conversation. A clean clone reproduces that. For example, `CMS_DEPLOY` will be unset there, as it will be for them.\n```\ngit clone https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms ~/mock-grade/iphs400-mp2-cms\ncd ~/mock-grade/iphs400-mp2-cms\n```\n\n## 3. Start a brand-new Claude Code session in that folder\n\nOpen a new terminal, run `cd` into the clone and start `claude`. Don't do it here: I've spent the whole day helping build this, so I'd grade with the same blind spots. Picking a different model with `/model`, such as Fable 5.1, gives a more independent second opinion, but it uses more of your limit.\n\n## 4. Give it this prompt\n\n```\nAct as the IPHS 400 MP2 grading agent. Follow docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nexactly: run worker tasks T0–T7 from section 10 and write the report in the\nsection 9 format. This is a rehearsal before submission:\n- Evaluate HEAD of main (the mp2-final tag does not exist yet; treat HEAD as the tag).\n- There is no email yet: score email-dependent items as null with the reason.\n- Pages URL: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n- Do not edit, commit or push anything in the repo, and do not publish or deploy.\n  Write the report to ~/mock-grade/report.md.\n- Never estimate: quote evidence for every score, and list every AI tell and\n  human tell you find (A3, A4).\nEnd with the 5 fixes that would gain the most points.\n```\n\n## 5. Bring the results back here\n\nPaste or point me to `~/mock-grade/report.md`. We'll fix what holds up, then commit, tag `mp2-final`, push, and send the email.\n\n## Things to expect\n\n- **The secret scan (D5) will find the demo passwords** printed in the session 15 transcript, and `PASSWORD=` lines in `.env.example`. Those are template defaults for a local-only console, and your report already admits the slip. Still, it'll show you how a grader reacts to it.\n- **The browser walkthrough (T3) needs Playwright,** and that only works now because you installed the libraries earlier. If it struggles, let it skip T3 and score C from the tests and screenshots, since you've already checked the app by hand.\n- **Cost and time:** a full T0–T7 run is a big job, probably 30–60 minutes and a sizeable share of a 5-hour window. {"parentUuid":"c8926671-7ce1-4bea-af26-3338993b8bf3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"05309790-5855-43f8-993d-28c4f0657e09","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"\n\n<pasted_content id=\"ff1a\">\nThis illustrates (1) metaprompting and (2) diff-driven goal setting\n\n\n\n1. here is the original first human hack prompt to create a\nsemi-autonomous 2-stage grader for MP#2:\n\nPROMPT #1:\n\n❯ 1. GOAL: Create the automated prepocessing stage of a 2 Stage\ngrading workflow framework where the first stage is an\n  LLMS judge automated grading of students repos against a given\nrubric. And the second stage is a human in the loop\n  clarification. Determination decision making over review of the\nautomated stage.\n  2. DOCUMENTATION: see the grading rubric in\n  ~/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter-dev/docs-archive/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nand the project description in the online\n  project repo in\nhttps://github.com/jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter/tree/main/docs\n  3. TEST_CASE: use the 2 submitted repos as test cases to build your\nautomated grading workflow (a)\n  https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms and (b)\nhttps://github.com/msgrespin/iphs400-mp2-cms\n  4. OUTPUT: based upon your analysis outputs in #1,2,3 generate a\ncanonical tech-spec in\n  dev/tech-spec_grader-2stage-hitl_v1_opus55high_20261001.md for\nimplementing this HITL-governmed 2 stage (first automated\n  LLM-as-judge using the rubric against the submitted github repoe\nthen second a high-leel HITL clarification/decision on\n  any unclear/fuzzy/reviews) as well as an Detailed, comprehensive,\nconcrete slash abstract actionable and well\n  structured manual with detailed step by step instructions.\nComprehensive listing of all resources used, URLs, GitHub\n  repos, et cetera, et cetera. in\ndocs/manual_grader-2stage-hitl_v1_opus55high_20261001.md\n\nPROMPT #2:\n\nrevise the last prompt to create a 2 stage semi-automated grading\nsystem to improve it to be more Complete, coherent, comma,\nconcrete/actionable and well structured.\n\nRESPONSE #2:\n\nHere's the revised prompt, ready to paste back or edit:\n\n---\n\nTask: Design a 2-stage, human-in-the-loop (HITL) grading system for\nIPHS 400 Mini-Project 2\n\n1. Goal\n\nDesign a semi-automated grading pipeline for student GitHub repos\nsubmitted for MP2 (CMS starter project):\n\n- Stage 1, the automated LLM-as-judge. For each submitted repo,\ncollect evidence and score every rubric criterion. Each score comes\nwith cited evidence, a confidence level and a flag that says whether a\nhuman needs to look at it.\n- Stage 2, the HITL review. I (the instructor) review only the\nflagged, unclear or borderline items. I confirm, override or clarify\neach one, and my decision is final. Every decision is logged with its\nreason.\n\nThe system should cut my grading time per repo by doing all the\nmechanical evidence gathering and clear-cut scoring. Every judgment\ncall that's fuzzy or high-stakes goes to me.\n\n2. Inputs (read all of these before designing anything)\n\n┌───────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│               Input               │\n  Location                                     │\n├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Grading rubric (authoritative)    │\n~/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter-dev/docs-archive/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\n │\n├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Project description /             │\nhttps://github.com/jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter/tree/main/docs\n         │\n│ student-facing docs               │\n                                               │\n├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Test submission A                 │\nhttps://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms\n         │\n├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Test submission B                 │\nhttps://github.com/msgrespin/iphs400-mp2-cms\n         │\n├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│ Starter template base commit      │ eaea7b1 in the starter repo (use\nit to separate student work from template      │\n│                                   │ code)\n                                               │\n└───────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n3. Required analysis (do this before writing the deliverables)\n\n1. Break the rubric into a list of criteria. For each one, record the\nID, points, the evidence it needs (files, commits, issues/PRs, labels,\ntests, deployed URL, docs) and whether it's objective (can be checked\nby a script), semi-objective (LLM judgment with clear anchors) or\nsubjective (always goes to a human).\n2. Compare the rubric with the project docs and list every ambiguity,\ngap or contradiction between them.\n3. Run a dry analysis of both test repos:\n   - diff each one against the starter base commit\n   - collect evidence for each criterion\n   - write a provisional score with citations\n   - list what would be flagged for Stage 2 and why\n\n   Use the results to justify the design. Don't post anything to the\nstudent repos.\n4. Check for the integrity hazard found in MP1: \"Sync fork\" can pull\nother students' commits into a repo. Commit authorship has to be\nattributed correctly, and any foreign commits must be flagged.\n\n4. Design requirements for the spec\n\nStage 1 (automated)\n- Ingestion: clone each repo pinned to the last commit before the\ndeadline, and record the SHA.\n- Deterministic pre-checks in Python that run before any LLM call:\nfile presence, tests passing, labels/issues present, commit history.\n- LLM judge: one call per criterion (or criterion group), with a fixed\nprompt template, the rubric anchors included verbatim, and structured\nJSON output containing score, max, evidence (file:line / commit SHA /\nURL), rationale, confidence (0–1) and flag reason.\n- Rules for routing items to Stage 2: low confidence, borderline\nscores, any subjective criterion, conflicting evidence, integrity\nanomalies, or the LLM disagreeing with a deterministic check.\n- Reproducibility: pinned model ID, temperature, saved prompt\nversions, and saved raw responses.\n- Cost and latency estimate per repo and per class of about 20 repos.\n\nStage 2 (HITL)\n- A review queue that contains only the flagged items, each showing\nits evidence and the LLM's rationale.\n- Decision actions: accept, override (with a score and a required\nreason) or request clarification from the student.\n- A simple interface. Recommend either a CLI or a generated\nMarkdown/HTML review sheet, and justify the choice.\n- An append-only audit log of every decision. Final grades come from\nmy decisions plus the Stage 1 items I didn't touch.\n- Output: a final grade sheet (CSV) and per-student feedback in Markdown.\n\nCross-cutting\n- Data model and file/folder layout for runs, evidence, judgments,\ndecisions and outputs.\n- A calibration step: grade both test repos by hand, compare the LLM\nscores against mine, and tune the prompts and thresholds until they\nagree.\n- Privacy: student data stays local apart from the LLM API calls, the\npipeline never writes to student repos, and no credentials go in\nfiles.\n- Tooling constraints: Python with uv, gh CLI for GitHub access,\nPodman if a container is needed, caches under /RESEARCH_SSD, no git\npush.\n\n5. Deliverables\n\n1. Tech spec at\ndev/tech-spec_grader-2stage-hitl_v1_opus55high_20261001.md, the\ncanonical design. Sections:\n   - goals and non-goals\n   - rubric→criteria mapping table\n   - architecture diagram (Mermaid)\n   - Stage 1 and Stage 2 designs\n   - data schemas (JSON examples)\n   - prompt templates\n   - routing thresholds\n   - audit and reproducibility\n   - risks and mitigations\n   - findings from the test-case dry run on both repos\n   - open questions for me\n   - an implementation plan with phases and acceptance criteria\n2. Operator manual at\ndocs/manual_grader-2stage-hitl_v1_opus55high_20261001.md, a\nstep-by-step guide I can follow on grading day. It covers:\n   - prerequisites and setup commands\n   - collecting the submission list\n   - running Stage 1\n   - reading the outputs\n   - working through the Stage 2 queue\n   - finalizing and exporting grades and feedback\n   - troubleshooting\n   - a worked example using test repo A\n   - a complete resources appendix: every file path, URL, GitHub repo,\ncommit SHA, model ID, CLI tool and doc that was used or referenced\n\n6. Constraints and acceptance\n\n- This task produces design and documentation only. Don't build the\ngrader code unless I ask in a separate step.\n- Never overwrite an existing file. If a target path already exists, write -v2.\n- Don't commit or push.\n- You're done when:\n  - both files exist\n  - every rubric criterion appears in the mapping table\n  - both test repos have dry-run findings in the spec\n  - every URL and path in the resources appendix resolves (show the\ncheck you ran)\n  - the spec's open-questions list is the only place unresolved decisions appear\n\n---\n\nWhat I changed and why:\n- Analysis before output. Your draft went straight to the\ndeliverables. The revised version makes the rubric breakdown and the\ndry run on both repos come first, so the design is based on real\nsubmissions.\n- Specific Stage 1 / Stage 2 split. It now says what makes an item go\nto a human and what a decision looks like. \"Unclear/fuzzy\" alone isn't\nsomething a pipeline can implement.\n- The Sync-fork authorship check from MP1. That's the integrity\nproblem most likely to come up again.\n- Starter base commit eaea7b1. The judge can then tell student work\napart from template code.\n- Scope and acceptance checks. The task is limited to design plus\nmanual, and there's a concrete definition of done.\n\nDo you want me to run this version now?\n\n✻ Baked for 33s · done 3:33 PM\n\n❯ yes, run it\n</pasted_content id=\"ff1a\">\n\nthis is something my professor sent us. {"parentUuid":"346452b7-a3e2-43ee-bf57-f45f0c3f1d6f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4bwKPrFtvqLWthGNTQh","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"It's a teaching example about **writing prompts**. It doesn't grade anything. There are three steps in it:\n\n1. **A rough first prompt.** Your professor wrote it quickly, typos and all, asking Claude to *design* a two-stage grading system: an AI judge scores each repo against the rubric (Stage 1), and the professor reviews only the unclear items (Stage 2).\n2. **Metaprompting.** Instead of running that rough prompt, they asked Claude to *rewrite the prompt itself* to be complete, concrete and well structured. Response #2 is that rewrite. It adds:\n   - inputs,\n   - required analysis before any writing,\n   - design requirements,\n   - deliverables,\n   - and a \"done when\" checklist.\n\n   It ends with \"What I changed and why\".\n3. **Running the improved prompt.** The output is two documents: a technical design and an operator manual for grading day. It says explicitly: \"design and documentation only. Don't build the grader code\".\n\n\"Diff-driven goal setting\" means comparing the rough prompt with the improved one and learning from the difference. The \"What I changed and why\" list is that comparison.\n\n**Should you use it to assess your work? Not as written.**\n- **It produces documents, not a grade.** You'd get a spec and a manual for building a grader, not scores for your repo.\n- **It's written for your professor's machine.** It points at their paths (`~/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter-dev`, `/RESEARCH_SSD`) and other students' repos as test cases. You shouldn't run anything against classmates' repos.\n- **It's expensive.** It asks for a full design across two repos, which is a large job, and your grace period ends tomorrow at 2:40 pm.\n\n**What it's useful for:** it shows how the real grader is likely to work, and two of its ideas are worth adding to your mock-grade prompt:\n- **Evidence, confidence and flags.** Every score comes with evidence, a confidence level, and whether a human would need to look at it. The items it would flag are your riskiest points.\n- **The authorship check against the starter template's base commit `eaea7b1`.** The grader separates your work from template code and flags commits by anyone else. Yours should be clean, because every commit is authored by you and Claude appears only as a `Co-Authored-By` line. Still, it's worth having the rehearsal confirm it.\n\nIt also mentions cloning each repo **\"pinned to the last commit before the deadline\"**. That design is from Oct 1, before the extension, and your rubric checks submission timestamps (H5). Make sure everything is pushed and tagged well before **Fri Oct 16, 2:40 pm**.\n\n**If you want to practise the technique itself,** do what your professor did: paste the mock-grade prompt I gave you into the fresh session, ask *\"revise this prompt to be more complete, concrete and well structured\"*, and run the revised version. Add these two lines to it first:\n```\n- For every rubric item, give evidence, a confidence (high/medium/low), and\n  whether a human grader would need to review it.\n- Check commit authorship against the starter base commit eaea7b1 and flag any\n  author other than me.\n```\n\nThat gives you a Stage-1-style rehearsal of your own repo, which is what you actually need before tagging `mp2-final`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3739,"cache_read_input_tokens":232773,"output_tokens":1705,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":621},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3739,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1705,"cache_read_input_tokens":232773,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3739,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3739},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"03c98a2b-62e3-4001-94f8-900a7555a975","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg4bwK5WUAp6HKtn1xWj4","requestRef":"5a07780d-31aa-4804-ba0a-452430315b6a","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"5a54c327-456c-43ca-b699-6d8a72179152","timestamp":"2026-10-15T19:50:10.229Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"3fe5d8d2-454b-407f-92b3-5945b5c07e19","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"aaca8758-60cb-4a64-807d-2c22a913a928","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

I've also saved it to a file so you can copy it without terminal line-wrapping:"},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011rjMavcghLpm4kh9XAcXSt","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/aaca8758-60cb-4a64-807d-2c22a913a928/scratchpad/mock-grade-prompt.md","content":"Task: Rehearse Stage 1 (the automated LLM-as-judge) of the IPHS 400 MP2 grading workflow on my own repo, before I submit\n\n1. Goal\n\nGrade this repo the way the instructor's automated Stage 1 grader would: collect evidence, score every rubric item, and route anything fuzzy to a \"needs human review\" list. Then tell me the fixes that would gain the most points before I tag `mp2-final`. This is a rehearsal. Nothing is submitted, and nothing in the repo changes.\n\n2. Inputs (read all of these before scoring anything)\n\n| Input | Location |\n|---|---|\n| Grading rubric (authoritative) | docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md: section 9 (report format), section 10 (worker tasks T0–T7), section 11 (deferral triggers) |\n| Project manual | docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md |\n| The repo under test | this clone, at HEAD of main (treat HEAD as if it were the `mp2-final` tag) |\n| Pages URL | https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ |\n| Report | docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_20261015.md |\n| Template base commit | The rubric names eaea7b1, but this repo was made with \"Use this template\", so that SHA is not in its history. Use this repo's first commit, a4605c6 (\"Initial commit\"), as the base, and record that substitution as a finding. |\n| Deadline | Fri Oct 16, 2:40 pm Eastern (end of the grace period). There is no submission email yet. |\n\n3. Order of work\n\n1. Pin the evaluation. Record the HEAD SHA and today's date. Every score refers to that SHA.\n2. Run the deterministic pre-checks before any judgment:\n   - `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2 --json`\n   - `uv run pytest -q`\n   - `git log --format='%an <%ae>' a4605c6..HEAD | sort | uniq -c`. Flag any author other than RafaelFrias1, because that is the \"Sync fork\" integrity hazard.\n   - `gh issue list --state all --limit 200 --json number,title,labels,createdAt,closedAt,body,comments`\n3. Work through T0–T7 from section 10 in order. For T3, start the server on port 8001, not 8000. Skip the Playwright walkthrough if it cannot run, and score C from the tests and docs/screenshots/ with confidence low.\n4. Score every item in sections A–H.\n5. Route items to the human-review list (section 6).\n\n4. For every rubric item, record\n\n- id, points, max\n- evidence: file:line, commit SHA, issue #, URL or a command output excerpt. Never estimate. If no evidence can be reached, set points to null and give the reason.\n- confidence: high, medium or low\n- a fix, whenever points < max: one concrete action I can take\n\nScore each item only on its own measure. Don't deduct twice for one flaw; cite the other item instead.\n\n5. Route to \"needs human review\" when any of these apply\n\n- confidence is low\n- the score sits on a boundary between two point levels\n- the item is subjective (A1, A3, A4)\n- two pieces of evidence conflict\n- a deterministic check and your judgment disagree\n- an integrity anomaly appears (authorship, a missing base commit, timestamps)\n- a section 11 deferral trigger applies\n\n7. Constraints\n\n- Read only. Do not edit, commit or push anything. Do not publish or deploy. Do not comment on, label or close issues.\n- Keep the clone's .env from .env.example. Never print passwords.\n- If something cannot be checked without the network or an account, mark it null instead of guessing.\n\n8. Output\n\nWrite ~/mock-grade/report.md in the section 9 format (front matter plus per-item rows), followed by:\n\n- a \"Needs human review\" table: item, why, and what a human should look at\n- \"Top 5 fixes before tagging\": each with its points at stake and the exact file or command\n\n9. You're done when\n\n- every item in sections A–H has a score or null with a reason\n- each of T0–T7 shows the command or evidence it was based on\n- the human-review table and the top-5 list exist\n- the repo is unchanged (`git status` is clean)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

Then tell me the fixes that would gain the most points before I tag `mp2-final`. This is a rehearsal. Nothing is submitted, and nothing in the repo changes.\n\n2. Seeding exits 1, no accounts exist, and every console capability fails (C1–C6, E4: \"runs clean from .env.example values with no manual steps\").\n2. **The admin console isn't usable on a phone** (F3, F4).\n   - Console pages below `/admin` request `style.css` from the wrong place, so they render unstyled.\n   - The editor's textarea overflows a 390 px screen.\n   - There is no nav between console screens.\n   - A save gives no confirmation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Settings read `.env` at the repo root when it exists. {"parentUuid":"2c9b59f1-77b1-4997-b70d-b232a4db44a5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4dxYLEoff5eiTCaHhi5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01M8Gm8njt98g9APLFckMYAd","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t08_grader_ready.py","content":"\"\"\"T08: grader-readiness (issue #9).\n\nThe rubric's grading run copies .env.example to .env and runs the seed script\nand the console with no other step, so settings must read .env themselves.\nThe console must also work on a phone: its own stylesheet, one nav on every\nscreen, and a message after a save.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nimport pytest\nfrom test_t03_posts import new_post\nfrom test_t04_publish import publish_new\n\nfrom app import settings\n\n\n# --- .env is read without a manual step --------------------------------------\n\ndef test_env_file_values_are_loaded(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    env = tmp_path / \".env\"\n    env.write_text('# a comment\\n\\nCMS_T08_PLAIN=one\\n'\n                   'CMS_T08_QUOTED=\"Kenyon Men\\'s Golf CMS\"\\n'\n                   \"export CMS_T08_EXPORTED='three'\\nnot a setting\\n\")\n    for key in (\"CMS_T08_PLAIN\", \"CMS_T08_QUOTED\", \"CMS_T08_EXPORTED\"):\n        monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)\n    settings.load_env_file(env)\n    assert os.environ[\"CMS_T08_PLAIN\"] == \"one\"\n    assert os.environ[\"CMS_T08_QUOTED\"] == \"Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\"\n    assert os.environ[\"CMS_T08_EXPORTED\"] == \"three\"\n\n\ndef test_real_environment_variables_win_over_env_file(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    env = tmp_path / \".env\"\n    env.write_text(\"CMS_T08_PLAIN=from-file\\n\")\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"CMS_T08_PLAIN\", \"from-shell\")\n    settings.load_env_file(env)\n    assert os.environ[\"CMS_T08_PLAIN\"] == \"from-shell\"\n\n\ndef test_a_missing_env_file_is_fine(tmp_path):\n    settings.load_env_file(tmp_path / \"no-such.env\")\n\n\ndef test_settings_read_env_with_no_sourcing_step(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"What the grader does: cp .env.example .env, then run Python directly.\"\"\"\n    env = tmp_path / \".env\"\n    env.write_text(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin\\nCMS_DEPLOY=on\\n\")\n    clean = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()\n             if k not in (\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\", \"CMS_DEPLOY\")}\n    out = subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, \"-c\",\n         \"import os; from app import settings; \"\n         \"print(os.environ['CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD'], settings.DEPLOY)\"],\n        env=clean | {\"CMS_ENV_FILE\": str(env)}, cwd=settings.ROOT,\n        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)\n    assert out.stdout.split() == [\"change-me-admin\", \"True\"]\n\n\ndef test_tests_never_read_the_developers_env_file():\n    assert os.environ.get(\"CMS_ENV_FILE\") == \"\"\n    assert settings.DEPLOY is False\n\n\n# --- the console on a phone --------------------------------------------------\n\nCONSOLE_PAGES = [\"/admin\", \"/admin/content\", \"/admin/posts/new\",\n                 \"/admin/accounts\"]\n\n\ndef test_every_console_page_loads_the_stylesheet_relatively(client_as, post_form):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    post_id = new_post(post_form, admin, \"Practice schedule\")\n    for path, css in [(\"/admin\", \"style.css\"), (\"/admin/content\", \"../style.css\"),\n                      (\"/admin/posts/new\", \"../../style.css\"),\n                      (f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", \"../../style.css\")]:\n        page = admin.get(path).text\n        assert f'<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{css}\">' in page, path\n\n\ndef test_the_stylesheet_keeps_form_fields_inside_a_phone_screen(client):\n    css = client.get(\"/style.css\").text\n    assert re.search(r\"textarea[^{]*\\{[^}]*max-width: 100%\", css)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", CONSOLE_PAGES)\ndef test_every_console_page_has_the_same_nav(client_as, path):\n    page = client_as(\"admin\").get(path).text\n    nav = re.search(r'<nav aria-label=\"Console\">(.*?)</nav>', page, re.S)\n    assert nav, path\n    for label in (\"Dashboard\", \"Content\", \"New post\", \"Accounts\", \"Log out\"):\n        assert label in nav.group(1), (path, label)\n\n\ndef test_editors_get_the_nav_without_admin_links(client_as):\n    page = client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin\").text\n    nav = re.search(r'<nav aria-label=\"Console\">(.*?)</nav>', page, re.S).group(1)\n    assert \"New post\" in nav and \"Log out\" in nav\n    assert \"Accounts\" not in nav and \"New page\" not in nav\n\n\ndef test_the_login_page_and_public_preview_have_no_console_nav(client):\n    assert 'aria-label=\"Console\"' not in client.get(\"/login\").text\n    assert 'aria-label=\"Console\"' not in client.get(\"/\").text\n\n\n# --- a save says it worked ---------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _status(html: str) -> str:\n    match = re.search(r'<p role=\"status\">(.*?)</p>', html, re.S)\n    return match.group(1) if match else \"\"\n\n\ndef test_saving_a_draft_says_so(client_as, post_form):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    response = post_form(c, \"/admin/posts\", title=\"Practice schedule\", body=\"\",\n                         action=\"save\")\n    assert \"Saved as a draft\" in _status(c.get(response.headers[\"location\"]).text)\n\n\ndef test_publishing_says_so_once(client_as, post_form):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    post_id = publish_new(post_form, c, \"Practice schedule\")\n    assert \"Published\" in _status(c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\").text)\n    assert _status(c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\").text) == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_saving_changes_and_unpublishing_say_so(client_as, post_form):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    post_id = publish_new(post_form, c, \"Practice schedule\")\n    c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\")\n    post_form(c, f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\", title=\"Practice schedule v2\",\n              body=\"\", action=\"save\")\n    assert \"Changes saved\" in _status(c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\").text)\n    post_form(c, f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}/unpublish\")\n    assert \"back to draft\" in _status(c.get(f\"/admin/posts/{post_id}\").text)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1929,"cache_read_input_tokens":270486,"output_tokens":4729,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":2084},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1929,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4729,"cache_read_input_tokens":270486,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1929,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1929},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01M8Gm8njt98g9APLFckMYAd":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t08_grader_ready.py","content":"\"\"\"T08: CMS_ENV_FILE names a different file, or \"\"\nfor none (the tests use that, so a developer's .env never reaches them).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef load_env_file(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy KEY=value lines from `path` into os.environ, unless already set.\n\n    Understands blank lines, # comments, an `export ` prefix and values in\n    single or double quotes, which is all .env.example uses.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return\n    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n        line = line.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n            continue\n        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n        key = key.removeprefix(\"export \").strip()\n        value = value.strip()\n        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in \"\\\\\"'\":\n            value = value[1:-1]\n        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n\n\n_env_file = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ENV_FILE\", str(ROOT / \".env\"))\nif _env_file:\n    load_env_file(Path(_env_file))\n\n'''\nassert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)\n\np='tests/conftest.py'; s=open(p).read()\nold='import re\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\n'\nnew='''import os\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n# Before any app import: settings must not read the developer's own .env\n# (its CMS_DEPLOY=on would make tests push to GitHub).\nos.environ[\"CMS_ENV_FILE\"] = \"\"\n'''\nassert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -n '\"\\\\\\\\' app/settings.py; uv run pytest -q tests/test_t08_grader_ready.py -k \"env\" 2>&1 | grep -E \"passed|failed\" | tail -2","description":"Add the .env loader; keep tests away from the real .env"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

The message is cleared after it is shown once.\n  \n  Vocabulary: \"Published\" and \"draft\" follow `CONTEXT.md`, and \"live\" and \"posted\" are not used. \"Unpublished\" is not a glossary term, but it matches the existing Unpublish action and is fine.\n  \n  Nothing in this category is wrong.\n</agent-message>"}

{"parentUuid":"cfe475c9-4dc5-417f-b0f6-e93ad9b18eea","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg4eQwP3uayoxKqVxk6yZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FTMGs7vQzZjcVppaVUBRG5","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"F=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-refiv-ubuncode-iphs400-mp2-cms/aaca8758-60cb-4a64-807d-2c22a913a928/scratchpad/t08-review.md && cat > $F <<'EOF'\n## /code-review findings for T08, and how each was resolved\n\nTwo reviews ran on the uncommitted work against 955eb84 (Standards and Spec, as separate sub-agents). Full suite after the fixes: `uv run pytest -q` → 212 passed.\n\n**Verified outside the tests,** in a clean copy of the working tree with no `.env` or `cms.db`:\n- The rubric's literal T3 steps work: `uv sync && cp .env.example .env`, then `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` (exit 0), then `uv run cms serve`. Admin login redirects to `/admin`.\n- At a 390 px viewport, `scrollWidth` is 390 on `/admin`, `/admin/content`, `/admin/posts/new`, `/admin/posts/4` and `/admin/accounts`.\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| The nav tests covered only 4 console pages, not the item edit page or the page routes. | **Fixed.** Added `/admin/pages/new`, `/admin/pages` and an item's edit page. |\n| The content list and accounts pages kept their own \"Back to…\" / \"New post · New page\" rows beside the nav. | **Fixed.** Removed. The item form keeps \"Back to posts\", which the nav doesn't cover. |\n| The nav adds \"New page\" for admins, which the ticket's list doesn't name. | Kept. It sits with Accounts as an admin-only link, and the dashboard already offered it. |\n| The console-only CSS rules ship in the public `style.css`. | Kept. The two share one stylesheet on purpose (one file, relative path). The rules are harmless on the public site and a comment says so. |\n| The test guard covers `.env` but not `CMS_DEPLOY=on` exported in a shell. | Accepted. The ticket names `.env`, and tests that build an app without a fake deployer never publish. |\n| All save messages were checked route by route; failed site updates show no success message. | No change needed. |\n\n### Standards\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| A `.env` line with an empty key (`=x`) crashed startup. | **Fixed.** Such lines are skipped. Test: `test_a_line_with_no_key_is_skipped`. |\n| One session key for the save message meant it could show on another item's page (two tabs). | **Fixed.** The message records its kind and item id, and only that item's page shows it. Test: `test_a_message_never_shows_on_another_items_page`. |\n| The console-nav regex was duplicated in the tests. | **Fixed.** Shared `_nav()` helper. |\n| Inline `# comments` after a value are kept as part of it. | Kept. The docstring scopes the parser to what `.env.example` uses, and `.env.example` has no inline comments. |\n| Importing settings changes `os.environ`. | Kept. That is how the rest of settings already reads its values. |\n| The paths in `base.html` come either as values passed in (public site) or from `root()` (console). | Kept, with a comment.
